title: What's changed for Drake Maye, New England Patriots as they look all the way back - CBS Sports
description: Don't look now, but the defending AFC champions have started to look more like themselves lately. After a tumultuous first three weeks o
body:
Don't look now, but the defending AFC champions have started to look more like themselves lately. After a tumultuous first three weeks of the 2026 campaign, where it looked like Mike Vrabel's club was enduring a hangover from the success they had a year ago, they've stabilized over the past two games and sit at 3-2 on the year. More than that, they seem primed to once again vie for the conference crown and make a bid for the Super Bowl. The biggest change, of course, has been Drake Maye. He was at the crux of New England's early-season struggles and has seen a night-and-day difference in his play over the past two weeks, especially when it comes to the turnover department. He's also coming off his first career back-to-back games with three-plus passing touchdowns. Drake Maye this seasonWeek 1-3Week 4-5Team PPG12.037.0Pass YPG195.0321.5Total TD18Turnovers72If you dig a little deeper into what's changed with Maye over these past two games, it's been the return of his deep ball. Last year, Maye was arguably the best deep-ball thrower in the NFL, but that effectively vanished at the start of this season — that sort of bled over from the offense's struggles last postseason. From Week 1-3, Maye was just 9-of-23 passing (39%) on throws of 15-plus air yards with no touchdowns and four interceptions. More recently (Week 4-5), Maye is 11-of-18 (61%) on those throws with three touchdowns and no interceptions. That efficiency has him right back to the range of where he was during the last regular season, where he completed 58% of such throws. If you remember, Maye finished second in MVP voting largely because of that prolific play down the field. If he's truly returned to that level, it makes his current odds to win MVP this season at +1700 quite tasty.  While Maye is the straw that stirs the drink of the entire organization, the Patriots' climb back up to their ceiling goes beyond his improved play over the past couple of weeks. The road ahead gets much easierComing into the year, the Patriots were facing a gauntlet out of the gate. New England had the hardest Week 14 strength of schedule by any team entering a season in the last 40 years. When you zoom out and look at it from 10,000 ft., the fact that they emerged from that at 2-2 is pretty solid. Of course, how they played in those games — and losing to a Seattle team that lost Sam Darnold after the opening drive — raised red flags, but from a record standpoint, it could've been much worse. They also picked up a key divisional win in Buffalo over that stretch, which is a valuable feather in their helmets as they look down the barrel of a schedule that does soften up. Patriots' remaining scheduleOpponentWeek 6vs. New York JetsWeek 7at Chicago Bears (Thursday Night Football)Week 8at Miami DolphinsWeek 9vs. Green Bay PackersWeek 10vs. Detroit Lions (in Munich, Germany)Week 11BYEWeek 12at Los Angeles ChargersWeek 13vs. Buffalo BillsWeek 14vs. Minnesota Vikings (Thursday Night Football)Week 15at Kansas City Chiefs (Monday Night Football)Week 16at New York JetsWeek 17vs. Denver BroncosWeek 18vs. Miami DolphinsThis week, they take on a 2-3 New York Jets team at home and are a touchdown favorite. Then, the Patriots head to Chicago on a short week, where they'll face a Bears team that is currently depleted. Caleb Williams (hamstring) is still sidelined, but could be back for that contest. However, standout running back Kyle Monangai (toe) is on the shelf, and defensive end Montez Sweat has been suspended for two games (including the matchup against New England) for violating the league's performance-enhancing substance policy. After their mini bye week, the Pats will visit the currently 0-5 Dolphins in Miami before a home matchup with a flawed Green Bay Packers team. Then, they will head off to Munich to face the Lions in Week 10. Detroit has one of the worst defenses in the NFL so far this season, so Drake Maye's affinity to chuck it deep could be on full display for the German fans. Given that path, it's conceivable that the Patriots enter the Week 11 bye on a seven-game winning streak, putting them at 8-2. Even if they drop a game or two, sitting at 7-3 or 6-4 at the well-positioned bye gives them a strong chance at double-digit wins. That would put them well within range of Buffalo in the AFC East race. For those wagering at home, the Patriots' win total currently sits at 10.5, with the Over priced at +120 on DraftKings. They're also +160 to win the AFC East and -370 to make the playoffs, so the oddsmakers are backing up what our eyes have been telling us these past two weeks. They're firmly in the mix. Looming return of A.J. Brown
Lost in the haze of Maye's resurgence is that he could be getting some massive reinforcements in the form of A.J. Brown. New England has yet to truly see any returns from their offseason prize after he suffered a high ankle sprain during the early portions of the team's Week 1 loss to Seattle. However, Brown is eligible to return from injured reserve as early as Week 6 against the New York Jets. Whenever he does come back, it adds a massive boost to an already emerging offense. Throughout the summer, the Patriots seemed to make a concerted effort to build the chemistry between Maye and Brown. I would theorize some of the early-season struggles we saw from Maye were due to him not having the best rapport with his other pass catches (notably free agent signee Romeo Doubs) because the team was focused on him working with Brown. Nevertheless, Brown brings a true No. 1 presence to the Patriots' passing attack, and the other weapons in the offense should now fit in quite well around him as he draws the eyeballs in coverage. Even in that brief window in Week 1, you saw the big play potential of Maye and Brown, with the wideout breaking loose on a flea-flicker. Maye wasn't able to put it on a streaking Brown, but the receiver was able to draw the DPI penalty to set up their lone touchdown of the game. 
Given Maye's rekindled mastery of the deep ball, injecting Brown into the equation could be like hitting the NOS to the offense. 
Pass rush gets surprising boost
One of my biggest concerns for the Patriots entering the season was their perceived lack of high-caliber play off the edge. That was particularly true after losing K'Lavon Chaisson in free agency and Harold Landy III beginning the year on injured reserve, where he still sits. Those were the top two sack leaders on the team a year ago, so it was a legitimate question as to where that production would come from. Well, through five weeks, the Patriots are ninth in the NFL in pressure rate thanks to the emergence of 2025 undrafted free agent Elijah Ponder and second-round rookie Gabe Jacas. Ponder has 4.5 sacks so far this season, which has him tied with T.J. Watt for the fifth-most in the NFL. Meanwhile, Jacas, who was slowed through the offseason due to injury and contract issues, has steadily started to ramp up as a legit presence off the edge. 
Gabe Jacas this seasonPressuresPressure rateTime to pressureWeek 1110%3.3 secondsWeek 239.4%2.8 secondsWeek 3310.3%2.6 secondsWeek 4321.4%2.9 secondsWeek 5417.4%2.7 secondsTheir ability to pressure the quarterback has been instrumental in that unit arguably improving from the one we saw last year.  Injuries are the biggest concern
The elephant in the room when it comes to New England truly reestablishing itself as a player in the AFC is, of course, injuries. While A.J. Brown going down in the opener was the headliner to begin the season, the injury bug has continued to take bites out of the team. Top cornerback Christian Gonzalez has missed the last two games with a shoulder injury, while fellow corner Carlton Davis also missed time with a neck ailment. On top of those hits to the secondary, the offense has had a number of injuries as well. Starting right guard Mike Onwenu suffered what is believed to be a season-ending ankle injury in Week 2 against the Steelers. The Patriots also recently placed wide receiver Mack Hollins (calf) and fullback Reggie Gilliam (ankle, knee) on injured reserve. Then, coming out of Week 5, starting left tackle Will Campbell suffered a knee injury, and running back TreVeyon Henderson went down with an ankle injury. Campbell reportedly sprained his MCL and is expected to miss some time. As for Henderson, he's expected to miss multiple weeks with a high ankle sprain. Those are some heavy hitters going down for New England, who will see its depth tested as it tries to continue making waves in the conference.

body:
Houston has gotten worse every year since its 2022 World Series and may finally be staring down a rebuild -- if Jim Crane allows it
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:28 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Houston Astros announced Wednesday that they have not renewed the contract of manager Joe Espada, expanding the leadership void atop the AL West winners and opening up questions about where owner Jim Crane sees this team going."We are thankful for Joe's hard work, his passion for the game, and for his commitment to the Houston Astros.  He represented the Astros and the Houston community in the most positive way. We wish he and his family the best moving forward," said Astros owner Jim Crane in a statement.For the last decade or so, the Astros have been reliable contenders and, for most of those years, a modern baseball dynasty. Since they emerged from their deep rebuild with a postseason berth in 2015, the Astros have hoisted the World Series trophy twice -- albeit with some scandal and controversy appended to one of those trophies -- won more than 100 games in a season on four occasions, and at one point made it at least as far as the ALCS for seven straight years. Now, though, these bedrock contenders are at a crossroads after seeing many members of that championship core depart over the years, and it may be that their window has finally closed. This can be wondered aloud not only because they were swept in the Wild Card Series by the Chicago White Sox, but also because the Astros in 2026, playoff berth notwithstanding, were a bad team. They finished the season with an 81-81 record despite having played, based on opponents' average winning percentage, the weakest schedule in all of MLB. That made them the only non-winning team in MLB history ever to make the playoffs in a full season. Additionally, the Astros had a -32 run differential during the regular season, which means they had a "deserved" record of 78-84. Again, a bad team. 
Now, they enter an uncertain offseason. The ongoing CBA negotiations hang over everything. General manager Dana Brown was let go in August and Crane named himself the temporary head of baseball operations. Espada is now out too. And beyond that, pervasive roster weaknesses mean it may not be advisable for the Astros to try to contend again in 2027. All of that sets the stage for the three questions that will, in many ways, define the Astros moving forward. Let's explore those now. 1. Who will be the new manager and head of baseball ops?This is the most central question of all. On the manager front, the leading "free agents" right now are, in no particular order, former Red Sox manager Alex Cora (the Astros' former bench coach under AJ Hinch), future Hall of Famer Albert Pujols, former Orioles manager Brandon Hyde, former Twins manager Rocco Baldelli, and former Cubs manager David Ross. Maybe current Astros bench coach Omar Lopez, a longtime presence in the organization, gets his shot. 
More important -- and much less clear -- is who will become the new general manager and/or president of baseball operations. Idly guessing specific names is a fool's errand when it comes to this kind of vacancy, so we won't do that. The Astros have some capable internal candidates who have been around since the Jeff Luhnow years, and that may be the path of least resistance. Otherwise, select assistant GMs or, in the case of a president of baseball operations search, GMs in other successful organizations will be under consideration. Is the job an attractive one? On one level, it's one of 30 such jobs in the world, and pretty much every front office employee with their hands in baseball ops aspires to such a role. So yes, it is. More specifically, though, the Astros are not in a good place right now. They're caught in a downward spiral on the field (they've gotten worse every year since winning it all in 2022), and the organization has fallen far behind in terms of player acquisition and development. Related to all that is the meddling presence of Crane and Astros-legend-turned-right-hand-advisor Jeff Bagwell. Let's explore that latter point more closely while wondering whether leading top-exec candidates might be turned off by the power dynamic in Houston. 
2. Will the new lead decision-maker have autonomy? Assuming the Astros don't opt to just rearrange their current front office structure -- which probably shouldn't be assumed, truthfully -- the new head of baseball ops needs the freedom to repair and reshape the organization. The problem is there's little reason to think that will be the case. Crane, when it comes to making actual baseball decisions, seems not to know all that he does not know, is far too hands-on, and has given too much power and influence to Bagwell, who's trenchantly anti-analytics at a time when the Astros need much more of that very thing. Crane, you'll recall, butted heads with James Click, Brown's predecessor, and fired him a week after the Astros won the World Series. Brown hardly distinguished himself, but how much was he truly allowed to implement his own vision for rebuilding the Astros' young talent base? That young talent base remains in a fairly wretched state. If Crane wants the top talent the Astros need in the big chair, then he can't do things like, oh, helm the talks that led to José Abreu's disaster contract or the Rafael Montero extension. The Astros need a new lead exec in baseball ops, but first, they need an owner who accepts he doesn't know as much as he thinks he knows. 
3. Is a rebuild ahead? Yes, it's tempting to go for it again in the sad-sack AL West, but the Astros, as repeatedly noted, are not good and, despite the MVP-grade presence of Yordan Alvarez, are almost certainly not going to be good anytime soon. This should lead to a rebuild that sees them pivot to the long-term and begin reconstructing the base of young, controllable talent. What would this mean? It might mean that whoever's in charge of the Astros -- putatively or in actuality -- opts to trade away select players with at least one year of control or contract remaining, like Josh Hader (assuming he's willing to waive his no-trade clause), Jeremy Peña, Isaac Paredes, Christian Walker, and, yes, maybe even Alvarez and Hunter Brown. No, the Astros don't necessarily need to go scorched earth and trade all of those core contributors, but most of them should be dealt in the name of setting the club up for future success. Will Crane allow such an approach? And if he does, will he allow his actual baseball people to make those crucial baseball decisions? That's to be determined.

body:
The most prolific quarterback in college football is a former zero-star prospect who spent 2025 playing for Mercer at the FCS level. Braden Atkinson has never ranked atop any high school or transfer rankings, but he might eventually rank atop the CBS Sports Quarterback Power Rankings.At this rate, anything is on the table for Atkinson, who leads the nation in touchdown passes with 21 and passing yards with an average of 373.7 per game. The last quarterback to average more yards over the course of a full season was 2023 Heisman Trophy winner Jayden Daniels.Atkinson has done it against quality opposition, too. Oregon State opened against Big 12 contenders Houston and Texas Tech, with Atkinson totaling nearly 800 yards passing across those two competitive losses. Since then, he's elevated even higher while leading Oregon State to four straight victories.Over the past two weeks alone, Atkinson has thrown for 836 yards with 10 touchdowns and no interceptions in blowout victories over San Diego State and Colorado State to help the Beavers establish themselves as contenders in the revamped Pac-12.
Atkinson's rise in this week's QBPR contrasts with Arch Manning's fall. The Texas quarterback is a former five-star prospect known to most college football fans by his first name. But after throwing a pair of interceptions in the fourth quarter of the Longhorns' loss to Oklahoma, Manning is taking a tumble in the QBPR.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Darian Mensah, MiamiMensah leads the nation in passing efficiency, completion percentage (84.2%) and EPA per dropback. He is one of just four Power Four quarterbacks who have attempted at least 100 passes without an interception. The Duke transfer also set new ACC records for consecutive completions earlier this season. He's been nearly perfect for the No. 3 Hurricanes. Last week: 1
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Braden Atkinson, Oregon StateAtkinson was named the Pac-12's Offensive Player of the Week for a third time after becoming the fourth FBS quarterback of the 21st century to throw for 400 yards, five touchdowns and no interceptions in consecutive weeks. His top target, Jesse Legree, leads the nation with 12 touchdown grabs, which is one more than Ohio State star Jeremiah Smith. Legree also holds an edge on Smith in receiving yards with 932 compared to Smith's 916. The man delivering the football has a lot to do with it. Last week: 12

                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Trinidad Chambliss, Ole MissChambliss enjoyed a light day in Week 6, as Ole Miss returned from a bye and hammered Vanderbilt 52-17. He totaled four touchdowns, bringing his tally through five games to 16. He ranks No. 8 nationally and No. 2 in the SEC in total yards per game at 309.6. This week brings a showdown with Missouri and quarterback Austin Simmons, whom Chambliss unseated at Ole Miss last year. Last week: 3
                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. CJ Carr, Notre DameIt's tempting to discount Carr as merely efficient and reliable, which he is. But Carr is also explosive, ranking fourth nationally in completions of 25+ yards with 19. That means 18.2% of his completions are going for 25+ yards. With Notre Dame traveling to BYU for a top-10 showdown this week, Carr will have one of his best chances to make a statement in the Heisman Trophy race. Last week: 4
                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Gunner Stockton, GeorgiaThankfully for Stockton, a potentially catastrophic interception was overturned late in the third quarter of Georgia's 20-17 win at Alabama, with the game tied. With that blunder erased, Stockton passed another huge test. He ranks No. 3 nationally in passer efficiency and is tied for second in the SEC with 14 passing touchdowns. As he showed on a 14-yard touchdown scamper against Alabama, he's also a threat to run. Last week: 5

                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. Josh Hoover, IndianaHoover threw a pair of touchdown passes in the fourth quarter to lead Indiana back from a 17-6 deficit at Nebraska. Now comes another huge test for the TCU transfer as Ohio State comes to town. Through six games, he is handling the unenviable task of replacing Fernando Mendoza with impressive effectiveness. Of the seven FBS quarterbacks with at least 100 attempts and no interceptions, none have thrown more touchdowns than Hoover with 17. Last week: 8
                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. Keelon Russell, AlabamaRussell orchestrated an impressive touchdown drive in the final two minutes of the first half in Alabama's eventual 20-17 loss to Georgia in Week 7. Georgia's strip-sack fumble of Russell on the game's first possession loomed large in the end, but the sophomore otherwise took care of the ball and didn't seem overwhelmed by the biggest challenge of his career. Last week: 2
                            
    
                                                
                    
    8. Drew Mestemaker, Oklahoma StateMestemaker is third in passing yards per game at 315 after turning in his fourth straight 300+ yard performance in Oklahoma State's 42-28 win over UCF.  The North Texas transfer is down to +4000 (DraftKings) to win the Heisman after coming in at +4500 last week. There is still some value there as Mestemaker is quarterbacking a top-20 program with Big 12 title aspirations. Last week: 7

                            
    
                                                
                    
    9. Julian Sayin, Ohio StateOf Sayin's 17 touchdown passes, 11 have gone to Jeremiah Smith. It would be interesting to take Smith away from the Ohio State offense and see how good Sayin -- or any other quarterback -- would look. After Smith's 916 receiving yards, the next-most productive receiver for the Buckeyes is Devin McCuin with 245 yards. The second-year starter ranks No. 4 in passer efficiency and is third in passing touchdowns. Last week: 6
                            
    
                                                
                    
    10. Devon Dampier, UtahDampier totaled four touchdowns and over 300 combined yards as a runner and passer in Utah's 41-24 win over Kansas in Week 6. Now in his second season with the Utes, Dampier has actually improved amid the coaching transition from Kyle Whittingham to Morgan Scalley. New offensive coordinator Kevin McGiven is deploying a creative system, and Dampier is thriving. Last week: 13
                            
    
                                                
                    
    11. Gio Lopez, Wake ForestLopez surpassed 300 yards passing for the third time this season as Wake Forest pulled away from NC State for a 38-14 win. The North Carolina transfer totaled four touchdowns -- three passing and one rushing -- in the win. His 1,680 passing yards are second in the ACC, and he ranks 15th nationally in EPA per dropback. Last week: 16

                            
    
                                                
                    
    12. Jayden Maiava, USCMaiava completed 21 of 33 passes for 301 yards and three touchdowns in USC's win at Penn State. He is 10th nationally in EPA per dropback as the Trojans enter a bye week. With top-15 foes Ohio State, Indiana and UCLA all still ahead on USC's schedule, Maiava will have the opportunity to make a Heisman push with some strong performances against quality opposition. Last week: 15
                            
    
                                                
                    
    13. Austin Simmons, MissouriSimmons is heading back to Ole Miss to play against Trinidad Chambliss, the quarterback who usurped him on the Rebels' depth chart last season. While the Ole Miss head coach and offensive coordinator jobs have changed hands since last season, this is still a chance for Simmons to make a statement. Simmons is less mobile than Chambliss, but he ranks ahead of him in passing efficiency and TD/INT ratio. Last week: 9
                            
    
                                                
                    
    14. Kamario Taylor, Mississippi StateTaylor's status for this week's game at LSU is uncertain due to a foot injury he suffered in a Week 5 loss to Alabama. Even after a shaky showing against the Crimson Tide, the talented sophomore ranks No. 8 nationally in passing yards per game (290) and No. 5 in total offense (321.8). He's got a cannon, he's a great runner, and he plays in a system that maximizes his potential. Last week: 10

                            
    
                                                
                    
    15. Anthony Colandrea, NebraskaWhen Colandrea shredded Indiana for a 39-yard touchdown run early in the fourth quarter to give Nebraska a 17-6 lead, he seemed on the precipice of superstardom. Then, Indiana mounted a comeback that took the wind from his sails. But his mobility and playmaking flair have undoubtedly upgraded the Nebraska offense. Last week: 14
                            
    
                                                
                    
    16. Conner Weigman, HoustonOne way or another, Weigman will get the job done. In a Week 5 win over UCF, he rushed for three touchdowns. Then, in a Week 6 victory at Kansas State, he threw for four. With 15 touchdowns and just one interception on the season, the former Texas A&M transfer is playing the best football of his career as the No. 20 Cougars enter a pivotal two-week stretch against Oklahoma State and Utah. Last week: 17
                            
    
                                                
                    
    17. Aidan Chiles, NorthwesternChiles is No. 7 nationally in passing efficiency and in yards per attempt (10.5) after throwing for 272 yards and three touchdowns in Northwestern's easy win over Ball State. Joining forces with first-year Wildcats offensive coordinator Chip Kelly is doing wonders to revitalize the career of the former four-star prospect. This week, he faces his former team as Northwestern travels to Michigan State. Last week: 18

                            
    
                                                
                    
    18. Noah Fifita, ArizonaFifita threw for a season-high 341 yards on a season-low 16 completions in Arizona's 52-31 Week 6 win at West Virginia. The chunk plays were flowing to the tune of 14.8 yards per attempt as Fifita tossed three touchdowns. He now leads the Big 12 in passer rating, passing touchdowns (16) and passing yards (1,756). Last week: 20
                            
    
                                                
                    
    19. Bear Bachmeier, BYUBachmeier threw for a season-high 329 yards and ran for a career-high 109 yards in BYU's 24-10 over Iowa State in Week 6. That made him the first BYU quarterback to go for 300/100 in a game since Taysom Hill in 2013. The Cougars will need another big performance from Bachmeier this week in a top-10 showdown with Notre Dame. Last week: 21
                            
    
                                                
                    
    20. Kevin Jennings, SMUJennings ranks No. 2 nationally in passing yards per game at 317.6 as he continues taking over the SMU record book. With the Mustangs quietly lurking in the ACC title race, the fifth-year star will have some legacy-defining moments ahead. Productivity has never been a problem for Jennings, but protecting the football has always been an issue. Last week: 19

The Wolverines are getting reinforcements after both players were granted a TRO, allowing for extra eligibility

        Michigan is getting some reinforcements just days before its game against Penn State. The Wolverines are adding former Miami tight end Alex Bauman and former Boise State cornerback Jeremiah Earby via the transfer portal, sources tell CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz.Both players were recently granted temporary restraining orders, giving them an extra season of eligibility, and they have enrolled at Michigan. Bauman and Earby played key roles for their respective teams last year, and they should give the Wolverines somewhat of a boost when the team needs it most.Bauman, a three-star prospect out of high school, spent the first three seasons of his career at Tulane before transferring to Miami last year. With the Hurricanes, Bauman earned a starting spot and totaled 18 receptions for 166 yards and a touchdown as the Hurricanes reached the national championship game.After the season, Bauman worked out at Miami's Pro Day but didn't secure an NFL roster spot, leaving the door open for him to return to college.Earby played two seasons at California but transferred to Boise State prior to the 2024 season. Earby was a key cog in the Broncos' defense last fall, and he earned second-team All-Mountain West honors while recording 60 total tackles and four interceptions.
Michigan searching for answersThese roster additions come at a time when Kyle Whittingham and his staff are searching for answers, particularly on offense. We don't know exactly what kind of roles Bauman and Earby will take on in the coming weeks, but it seems like the former could get a real shot to make his mark.The Wolverines' passing offense ranks last in the Big Ten, which means they could try to lean on the run game more in the second half of the season. If that is the case, Bauman could get his chance in a couple of areas. If Michigan decides to go with heavier personnel, Bauman would be a candidate to get some playing time in multiple tight end sets.On top of that, Michigan has gotten next to nothing out of its tight ends in the receiving game. Their leading receiver at that position is Hogan Hansen, who has five catches for 35 yards. Can Bauman provide the semblance of a receiving threat at that spot?
As for Earby, he may have a tougher time carving out a big role for himself. Michigan has the best pass defense in the Big Ten, allowing just 146.8 yards per game. The former Boise State cornerback may just find himself in the defensive back rotation, but more depth never hurts. Plus, Michigan is in no position to snub its nose up at difference-makers, no matter when and where it adds that player.

The youngest son of LeBron James redshirted during his freshman season with the Wildcats and is expected to be part of Arizona's rotation this season.

        Arizona played its first exhibition game of the 2026-27 college basketball season on Tuesday, marking the first time projected top-three pick in the 2027 NBA Draft Caleb Holt faced college competition. Holt was in Arizona's starting lineup next to Motiejus Krvias, Ivan Kharchenkov, North Carolina transfer Derek Dixon and Bryce James, the youngest son of current Philadelphia 76ers star and NBA superstar LeBron James.James, who redshirted during his freshman season, appeared in two exhibition games during the 2025-26 season, but Arizona's 93-69 win over San Francisco marked his first start. James started the game by knocking down a corner 3-pointer and finished the game with three points and a steal in 14 minutes of action.
Clemson transfer RJ Godfrey, who is seeking a fifth year of eligibility, didn't play in Arizona's exhibition game. His status remains unclear with the season less than three weeks away. If Godfrey is cleared, he projects as Arizona's starting power forward.After the game, Arizona coach Tommy Lloyd was asked directly why he started James instead of going with a smaller lineup.
"I didn't want to overthink it," Lloyd said. "Bryce has had a good fall for us and continues to grow as a player. I think starting Bryce kinda puts the rotation in the right way and maybe have some good impactful guys coming off the bench. I kinda wanted to see how that looked and felt today. I don't know what I'm going to do Friday (against San Diego State). ... Again, I'm not going to overthink that one. It's the first few minutes of a 40-minute game."JJ Mandaquit, Cameron Holmes and Maksim Brnovic played more minutes off the bench than James against San Francisco. However, James started two of Arizona's three games during the program's Lithuanian tour earlier this summer and is set to earn a rotation role with the projected Big 12 favorite.James was part of Arizona's loaded 2025 recruiting class that helped the Wildcats reach the Final Four for the first time since 2001. James committed to Arizona on New Year's Day in 2025, just a few months before Koa Peat and Brayden Burries — two players drafted in the first round of the 2026 NBA Draft — pledged to play for the Wildcats.
Peat told CBS Sports at the Final Four in April that James played a role in getting him to commit to Arizona."He hit me up and told me to go to school together," Peat said. "So obviously, yeah. When guys like that come to Arizona, it's super cool. It definitely could have an impact on your recruitment for sure."Holt shows why he will be an early pick in 2027Arizona's returning duo of Krivas and Kharchenkov is among the best in the sport, but the key newcomer on the roster is primed to be Holt. The No. 3-ranked player in the 2026 recruiting cycle by 247Sports is expected to be in the conversation as the best first-year player in the sport because of his ability to impact the game on both ends of the floor.
Holt finished with 17 points, five rebounds, two assists and three steals in 28 minutes of action. He also finished an efficient 6 of 10 from the field and knocked down all four of his free throw attempts.The play of the night that stood out was during the opening minutes of the second half, when Holt got a steal near the 3-point line and went coast-to-coast for a tough bucket in transition on the other end. Holt, who is listed at 6-foot-5, 215 pounds, used his strength to his advantage on the play to create separation against a bigger defender, which is something he should be able to do often.
"Caleb is really motivated to be a great all-around player," Lloyd said. "And to really understand the nuances of the game. He has really shouldered the heavy burden on his own of trying to learn. You are talking about a guy who has risen through the ranks at the highest levels of high school basketball and international basketball with his effort and raw instincts. Now he's trying to refine himself a little bit. ... He's a really skilled and unique player."
Arizona has two scrimmages (San Diego State on Friday and Eastern Washington on Oct. 23) before opening the 2026-27 campaign against UCLA in Las Vegas. That game will feature two of the best freshmen in the sport in Holt and UCLA star Nikola Kusturica, facing each other head-to-head. While Holt projects as an early pick in the 2027 NBA Draft, Kusturica is ineligible for this summer's draft due to the NBA's age requirement.

title: 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America Teams: Thomas Haugh, Jeremy Fears Jr., Tyran Stokes among top stars - CBS Sports
description: For all of the debates tied to revenue-sharing, big NIL deals, loosened eligibility rules, transfer-waivers and the supposed "chaos" tho
body:
For all of the debates tied to revenue-sharing, big NIL deals, loosened eligibility rules, transfer-waivers and the supposed "chaos" those things have combined to bring to college athletics, there's no denying that changes to the system, dramatic as they might be, are keeping elite talent in school longer.This upcoming season is a reminder.The CBS Sports All-America teams are evidence.In any other era of the sport, players like Florida's Thomas Haugh, Vanderbilt's Tyler Tanner, Texas Tech's JT Toppin and Virginia Thijs De Ridder, just to name a few, would no longer be in college -- and De Ridder probably would've never even enrolled considering he's a former professional from Belgium. As it is, though, each of them is an established college star who has passed on professional opportunities to either enroll in school or stay in school (or both), and they were all voted by a panel of writers and analysts to one of the three 2026-27 CBS Sports preseason All-America teams.Haugh and Tanner, among the favorites to be SEC Player of the Year, were joined on the FIrst Team by Michigan State point guard Jeremy Fears Jr., Kansas freshman Tyran Stokes and Illinois sophomore David Mirkovic. That means 40% of the First Team comes from either the Big Ten or SEC, which shouldn't be surprising considering those are the two wealthiest conferences.Fears and Haugh were unanimous first-team selections.Toppin was voted Second Team despite the possibility that he won't be available to start the season after tearing the ACL in his right knee last February. The 6-foot-9 forward was the 2025 Big 12 Player of the Year.
The only school from outside of the Power Four (football term) with a CBS Sports preseason All-American is UConn (Silas Demary). Here's the conference breakdown of the three All-America teams:Big 12: 4SEC: 4ACC: 3Big Ten: 3Big East: 1Note: The 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America Teams were voted on by college basketball reporters at CBS Sports, 247Sports and analysts and on-air talent from CBS and CBS Sports Network.  
        
            
                Best of the rest: Pac-12 returns, Mountain West shifts, new leagues, college hoops Cinderellas to know
                
                    Matt Norlander                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
CBS Sports Preseason All-America First Team
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jeremy Fears Jr. | PG | Michigan State | 6-2 | R-Jr.Fears is a wizard playmaker who led all of college basketball in assists (9.4 per game) last season. Fears' 53.1 assist rate was the best mark in the last two decades, according to KenPom.com, and he flirted with a mind-boggling 4-to-1, assist-to-turnover ratio. No Big Ten player has ever averaged more than 10 assists in a single season, but Fears could change that and put his name in the Big Ten record books forever.
Fears' creation is vital for Michigan State's outlook in 2026-27, but if he can take one more surge as a shot-maker, the Spartans can start dreaming of winning six in a row. Fears' jumper has gotten better every year, and if that trend sticks, Fears is on the verge of a historic season. -- Isaac Trotter
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Thomas Haugh | SF | Florida | 6-9 | Sr.Haugh's rise from no-name, three-star prospect to a preseason All-American is special stuff. The 6-9 forward passed on a first-round grade from NBA decision-makers to cash in on a lot money to be the face of Florida basketball. Haugh could easily average 17-and-6 again for a loaded Gators squad that is the sturdiest preseason No. 1 outfit we've seen in years. Haugh's energy is a constant. He's an awesome transition scorer who can make hay as a cutter, slasher and real-deal defender. If Haugh can go from 32% to 38% from 3-point range and improve his on-ball potency, he will solidify himself as a lottery pick in a wide-open 2027 NBA Draft. -- IT
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Tyler Tanner | PG | Vanderbilt | 6-0 | Jr.Tanner is an outlier of all outliers. He's a shade under 5-11 barefoot. He wasn't a ballyhooed recruit. He's also incredible. Tanner is a big-time athlete who jack-hammered 17 dunks, becoming just the third high-major guard who is 6-foot or shorter to reach that threshold in the Bart Torvik database, which stretches back to 2008. 
But his superpowers stretch beyond just creating dunks at a historical rate. The lightning-quick point guard just does not make mistakes. He posted a 2.5-to-1 assist-to-turnover rate this past season. He creates advantages offensively in his sleep using speed and a nasty change of direction. There was a play against Nebraska in the NCAA Tournament where Tanner de-pantsed three defenders with three separate crossovers on his way to the cup. Oh, and he defends. And rebounds. And draws fouls. And makes tough shots. And runs his team. Like Thanos (and Cameron Boozer last season), Tanner is inevitable. -- IT   
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Tyran Stokes | PF | Kansas | 6-8 | Fr.College basketball's most naturally gifted player will lace 'em up for the Jayhawks. Stokes is on the inside track to be the No. 1 pick in the 2027 NBA Draft because he can blend excellent positional size with real on-ball utility. Stokes is all of 6-7 and 230 pounds. He will bully smaller defenders and dust heftier defenders. Stokes' big-boy drives will be a staple of Kansas' offense, and he should automatically vault to the top of the charts in transition scoring. Stokes' maturity and on-court antics have long been a point of emphasis, but if Bill Self can help his star freshman stay on the straight and narrow, he has a chance to be a terrifying two-way player who could up some bonkers counting stats as Kansas' head honcho. An average stat line of 20 points, eight rebounds and three assists is firmly in Stokes' range of potential outcomes. -- IT   

                            
    
                                                
                    
    David Mirkovic | PF | Illinois | 6-9 | Soph. Illinois' razor-sharp offense has produced a string of All-Americans like Ayo Dosunmu, Kofi Cockburn, Terrence Shannon Jr. and Keaton Wagler. Brad Underwood believes Mirkovic could be up next. The burly 6-9 forward sees the game at an advanced level, and his physicality, competitiveness, feel and 3-point shooting are all extremely attractive traits. Mirkovic used maniac rebounding to become a Day 1 starter for Illinois, despite being just a teenager in a new country, but the Montenegro native has transformed into a true offensive hub who can initiate pick-and-rolls or play in backdowns to create advantages. Mirkovic was the third-best freshman in the Big Ten last year behind two lottery picks in Wagler and Washington's Hannes Steinbach. Now, it's his turn.Mirkovic is slowly but surely working his way back from an offseason foot surgery, but he's positioned to be one of the top big men (and interviews) in all of college ball. -- ITCBS Sports Preseason All-America Second Team
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Motiejus Krivas | C | Arizona | 7-2 | Sr.Krivas is primed to elevate his game even higher after a breakout junior season in which he started all 39 games while shining as a paint protector for a Final Four team. The towering Lithuanian is the Big 12's leading returning shot blocker and a rugged rebounder. 
His offensive repertoire isn't particularly robust, but Arizona doesn't need him to be Nikola Jokic. The Wildcats need size, physicality and production, which he brings in abundance as one of the nation's most-proven bigs. -- David Cobb
                            
    
                                                
                    
    JT Toppin | PF/C | Texas Tech | 6-9 | Sr.Toppin earned multiple All-American honors last season, even after suffering a season-ending ACL injury in mid-February. The 6-9 senior is tracking for a midseason return (if not before Christmas, potentially) and should quickly reclaim his place as one of the nation's top interior scorers.Before his injury, Toppin averaged 21.8 points, 10.8 rebounds and 1.7 blocks on 54.8% shooting. Toppin is a matchup nightmare for many teams because he's too agile and athletic for many opposing 5 and too strong for many opposing 4s. -- DC

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Silas Demary Jr. | PG | UConn | 6-4 | Sr.Demary gritted through injuries during UConn's postseason run after proving himself to be an ideal fit to run point for Dan Hurley during his first season with the Huskies. The Georgia transfer transformed into a pass-first floor general with UConn, leading the Big East with 5.9 assists per game. Demary also brings great size to his position, which helps make him UConn's best perimeter defender. Demary was fifth in scoring for the Huskies last season at 10.1 points per game, but his all-around value is significantly deeper than his own offensive production. -- DC    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Flory Bidunga | PF/C | Louisville | 6-9 | Jr.Bidunga ranked as the No. 1 transfer of the cycle after earning Big 12 Defensive Player of the Year and all-conference honors at Kansas as a sophomore. Now, he is joining a Louisville program in need of the physicality and front court pop that Bidunga provides in abundance. 
At 6-9 and 235 pounds, Bidunga brings a level of productivity and star power to the paint that was missing from coach Pat Kelsey's first two teams. He's an excellent lob threat and a versatile defender with the agility to switch and recover. -- DC
                            
    
                                                
                    
    John Blackwell | SG | Duke | 6-5 | Sr.After leading Wisconsin in scoring at 19.1 points per game as a junior, Blackwell is taking his bucket-getting powers to a Duke program that lost leading scorers Cam Boozer and Isaiah Evans. The fourth-year guard will get plenty of spot-up opportunities just like Evans did a year ago.Regardless of where he ultimately falls in the scoring hierarchy for a loaded Duke team, Blackwell will be called upon to hit big shots and make plays offensively. A three-year body of work at Wisconsin suggests he'll be up to the task. -- DC
CBS Sports Preseason All-America Third Team
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Thijs De Ridder | PF | Virginia | 6-9 | Soph.De Ridder, 23, was named the preseason ACC Player of the Year by CBS Sports and is one of the most experienced players returning to the conference. The Virginia forward averaged 15.6 points, 6.2 rebounds and 1.6 assists during his freshman season. The 23-year-old forward previously played for Bilbao Basket (2023-25) and Antwerp Giants (2020-23) before arriving in the States to play college basketball. After a 30-win season in Year 1 of Ryan Odum's tenure, expectations are high at Virginia. -- Cameron Salerno
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Elliot Cadeau | PG | Michigan | 6-1 | Senior Cadeau completed one of the best redemption stories in college basketball after being named Most Outstanding Player at the Final Four. Cadeau, who began his career at North Carolina, is a crucial returning starter from Michigan's national title roster and is one of the most experienced and productive players returning to the sport. He averaged 10.5 points and 5.9 assists last season with the Wolverines and will be Mike Boynton's most trusted piece in the wake of Dusty May leaving for the Mavericks. -- CS
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Milan Momcilovic | SF/PF | Kentucky | 6-9 | Sr. Momcilvoic was the best 3-point shooter in college basketball last season and knocked down 136 3-pointers, while shooting 48.7% from beyond the arc. After exiting Iowa State, he was considered one of the most coveted players in the transfer portal. Kentucky landed him -- and had to pay a pretty penny in the process -- but it gave the Cats a true star who should be a perfect fit in Mark Pope's expressive offensive system. -- CS

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Robert Wright III | PG | BYU | 6-1 | Jr. Wright entered the transfer portal earlier this offseason, then withdrew and returned to BYU. Wright is coming off a season in which he averaged 18.1 points and 4.6 assists during his first season with the Cougars while playing the Robin role next to eventual No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa. The former Baylor star is one of the top bucket-getters in the sport and figures to see his usage rise. -- CS
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Rueben Chinyelu | C | Florida | 6-10 | Sr. Florida is the only team with two preseason All-America honorees. The reigning Naismith Defensive Player of the Year is part of a massive and intimidating Florida frontline. Chinyelu was one of 14 players in Division I who averaged a double-double (10.9 points, 11.2 rebounds) last season. Chinyelu has been a full-time starter in each of the last two seasons for the Gators. Florida earned a No. 1 seed in the NCAA Tournament both times with Chinyelu as a starter. -- CS

body:
Denver's offense ranks near the bottom of the NFL, but its history of wild second-half comebacks shows why Nix's strange comments hold some truth
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026

    9:35 am ET

            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Denver Broncos are off to a 3-2 start this season, but it's been a pretty rocky 3-2 start if we are being honest. The offense ranks third-worst in the entire NFL, averaging just 269.0 total yards per game, and Sean Payton has already yanked play-calling duties away from new offensive coordinator Davis Webb.The play-calling change didn't help on Sunday, as the Broncos struggled against the winless Los Angeles Chargers. Denver did escape SoFi Stadium with a 23-17 victory, but the offense put up just 224 total yards and converted one of 12 third downs while quarterback Bo Nix threw for 123 yards and a touchdown.Nix doesn't look like a quarterback on the cusp of leading the Broncos to the Super Bowl nine months ago. He's completed 59.9% of his passes, which ranks 26th in the NFL, and his 188.4 passing yards per game rank 25th. While Denver added a deep threat in wide receiver Jaylen Waddle this offseason, Nix's 5.2 air yards per attempt are the fewest by a qualifying quarterback through five games since C.J. Beathard's 5.1 in 2018.But Nix doesn't seem overly worried about it. During Tuesday's press conference, Nix was asked how he handles stretches when he's playing well and when he's not. What's his process like when it comes to moving on from bad plays? He offered a pretty strange response. 
"It's the same when I'm playing really good," Nix responded. "I think playing good and playing bad, it's a narrative, and I think it's honestly kind of something we make up. I don't think necessarily I'm playing any different than what I'm normally playing it's just every once in a while a ball will bounce this way or something will happen this way and we'll get a pressure on this look when we had somebody open, I had to throw it away and I wanted to hold onto it a little bit longer and the guy was open and next thing you know, statline looks different. We're talking about something completely different..."Playing good and playing bad is a narrative? It's something we make up? How can that be true?This is one of those strange cases where the messenger actually makes the message make more sense. Because we've seen Nix play "good" and "bad" football in the span of 60 minutes many times over the last three years. That's how the Broncos have the most comeback wins (15), second-half comebacks (12) and fourth-quarter comebacks (8) in the NFL since 2025. 
Take what happened in Week 3, for example. The Broncos were hosting Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams on "Sunday Night Football" and had an embarrassing first half, going down 16-0. However, like we've seen Nix and the Broncos do so many times before, they bounced back in the second half and scored a whopping 30 points to register another come-from-behind victory. It was Denver's third comeback win of 14+ points over the last two seasons, the most in the NFL.Broncos Week 3 vs. RamsFirst halfSecond halfPoints030Opponent points1610Nix total yards57136So, did Nix play "good" or "bad" football vs. the Rams? It was both! It's not necessarily one or the other.What has to be said is that the Broncos need to find a way to be consistent, because they would be a legitimate contender if they could play 60 minutes the way they usually play the final 30. Denver has the pieces to make a postseason run once again. Remember, if Nix hadn't injured his ankle in the divisional round vs. Buffalo, the Broncos had a great chance to represent the AFC in Super Bowl LX. Coach Payton has to find a way to get the most out of his offense, and he has a tough test ahead of him this week, as the Broncos welcome the Seattle Seahawks and their top-ranked defense to town on Thursday night.

title: NBA rookie impact rankings: 10 first-year players who will make presence felt immediately - CBS Sports
description: Entering the 2025-26 college basketball season, the hype around the incoming freshmen class was palpable. Led by the likes of Darryn Pet
body:
Entering the 2025-26 college basketball season, the hype around the incoming freshmen class was palpable. Led by the likes of Darryn Peterson, AJ Dybantsa, Cameron Boozer and Caleb Wilson, that group departed college basketball as one of the best freshmen classes of this generation.Now, as those players enter their rookie seasons in the NBA, there is even more hype surrounding what could be one of the best rookie classes this century. Peterson and Dybantsa are joining unique situations: the Jazz and Wizards both missed the playoffs, but there is infrastructure in place for those teams to make a huge jump this season. Peterson and Dybantsa won't have to shoulder the load of being the guy from Day 1.Because of how deep this class is, other players throughout the lottery are set for a significant role immediately. One name to watch is Kings guard Darius Acuff Jr., who will be handed the keys to Sacramento's offense immediately. Acuff was an All-American during his one-and-done season at Arkansas and was the best true point guard in the sport.Outside of the top 10 picks, Warriors forward Yaxel Lendeborg — the oldest player drafted in the first round — should get an opportunity to start from Day 1. With Kristaps Porziņģis' status in limbo to begin the season, Lendeborg's number will be called on even more than anticipated.
With the season on the horizon, here are the 10 rookies who could make a significant impact for their respective teams. All rookie of the year odds are via FanDuel Sportsbook.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Cameron Boozer, GrizzliesOdds to win Rookie of the Year: +300Boozer was comfortably the best player in college basketball last season. He went No. 3 to the Grizzlies anyway because Peterson and Dybantsa were in the same draft class. Boozer probably goes No. 1 in most years, but not in 2026.What makes Boozer so good? It's a combination of his elite basketball IQ, passing and rebounding. Boozer is a bruiser down low who uses pump fakes to draw contact to get to the line. Boozer attempted 280 free throws at Duke last season, which ranked No. 4 among all Division I players. I'm comfortable with saying that Boozer will be the best rookie in the league this season because of his floor and projected role. He can be a 20/8 player as a rookie.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Darryn Peterson, JazzOdds to win Rookie of the Year: +350Peterson had a roller coaster of a freshman season at Kansas. After entering last fall as the projected No. 1 pick in the 2026 Draft, Peterson was sidelined for nearly a dozen games due to cramping issues. When Peterson was on the floor, he showed why he was one of the best guard prospects of this era. Peterson's shotmaking ability is second-to-none in this class. What should be interesting to see this year is how Peterson plays on the ball in an experienced Utah lineup. In high school, Peterson's on-ball usage rate was high. At Kansas, however, it was less apparent. Peterson should thrive as a shooter in his rookie season and has a chance to make a real impact. My semi-hot take entering the year is that Utah finishes top six in the West, with Peterson playing a huge part in that leap.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. AJ Dybantsa, WizardsOdds to win Rookie of the Year: +410The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft is joining a Washington team that has had an interesting last 10 months. The Wizards bought low on Trae Young and Anthony Davis to pair with their young core and now, after winning the lottery and landing Dybantsa, finishing in the top 10 of the loaded Eastern Conference shouldn't be out of the question.
As mentioned earlier, Boozer ranked No. 4 among all Division I players in free-throw attempts. Dybantsa ranked first in that category while playing in three fewer games. Dybantsa is exceptional at getting to the free-throw line. He is able to draw contact with his bendy frame, which allows him to find space against defenders on drives to the hoop. He is also an incredible mid-range shooter. If his 3-point shot improves, it will be a game-changer.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. Caleb Wilson, BullsOdds to win Rookie of the Year: +340Wilson's freshman season at North Carolina was cut short after two separate hand injuries. If he doesn't get hurt, he is probably a first-team All-American. That's how good he was. Wilson was one of the best dunkers in college basketball last season and ranked near the top of the country in that category.Wilson's swing skill in the NBA will be 3-point shooting. At UNC, he attempted just 27 3-pointers and made only seven. However, during summer league and throughout the preseason, Wilson has been taking more shots from beyond the arc. If the shooting is real, it completely changes his ceiling. Wilson should be an interesting ROTY candidate because his usage rate could be higher than that of many on this list.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Darius Acuff Jr., KingsOdds to win Rookie of the Year: +1000In our way-too-early Rookie of the Year predictions, I went with Acuff. If someone picked outside of the top four has the most realistic chance of winning the award, it's him for a few reasons. The most obvious one is that his usage rate on a given night will be higher than almost anybody in this class. The Kings are handing Acuff the keys to the offense, and he should benefit tremendously from playing next to Domantas Sabonis, who is one of the best screeners in the NBA. That duo was on full display during Sacramento's preseason opener against the Lakers, when Sabonis set hard screens for Acuff and allowed the former Arkansas star to find open space to create. Acuff has a real shot to average close to 20/5 during his rookie year, which should keep him in the ROTY race.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. Yaxel Lendeborg, WarriorsOdds to win Rookie of the Year: +1500One of the biggest mysteries entering the season is the status of Porziņģis, who is dealing with a mystery illness and has no timeline for a return. If he misses extended time, expect Lendeborg to be in Golden State's starting lineup on opening night. And even when Porziņģis returns, Lendeborg is versatile enough to slot anywhere in the frontcourt. 
Lendeborg has experience playing next to two other bigs. At Michigan, Dusty May started Lendeborg, Aday Mara, and Morez Johnson Jr. to form a terrifying frontcourt that gave opponents fits. Lendeborg is one of the most NBA-ready rookies in the class and could make an immediate impact.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. Mikel Brown Jr., NetsOdds to win Rookie of the Year: +2500Brown has yet to appear in the preseason due to an ankle injury, but could make his debut on Wednesday against the Wizards. Brown's freshman season at Louisville was a mixed bag. When he played, he showed why he has the potential to be the best true point guard in the class. However, he missed 14 games last season due to a back issue, including Louisville's final two NCAA Tournament games.Brown's strength is his 3-point shooting. He has serious NBA range, and the raw shooting stats (34.4% on 7.6 attempts) don't tell the full story. Brooklyn's backcourt fit of Brown and Egor Dёmin complements each other well.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    8. Aday Mara, ThunderOdds to win Rookie of the Year: +25000Mara is heading to an ideal situation where he should play spot minutes on an NBA title contender. He isn't going to start and probably won't even crack 22 minutes per night off the bench, but he stands to make a significant impact when he does play.Mara was one of the best shot blockers and the most efficient scorers in college basketball in terms of field-goal percentage: he blocked 2.6 shots per game and converted on 66.8% of his attempts, with 291 of the 301 total field goal attempts coming from inside the arc. Mara is also a very good passer for his size.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    9. Keaton Wagler, ClippersOdds to win Rookie of the Year: +4000The Clippers are entering a new era after trading away Kawhi Leonard. After watching the ping pong balls go their way during the NBA Draft Lottery, the Clippers got the fifth pick and passed on Acuff and Brown to select Wagler, who went from unknown recruit to a consensus first-team All-American.
Wagler got off to a slow start in summer league but finished strong. He will likely come off the bench, at least to start his rookie season, but he should be able to run L.A.'s second unit when on the floor. Wagler projects as a very good shooter for his size and should contribute in that area when on the floor.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    10. Kingston Flemings, HawksOdds to win Rookie of the Year: +10000Flemings, the No. 8 overall pick in the draft, had a terrific one-and-done season at Houston. He was as good as anybody in college basketball at getting to his spots in the mid-range area. Think De'Aaron Fox from when he was at Kentucky and just starting his career with the Kings.Flemings' ability to use his speed as a change of pace or get downhill is impressive. He will likely come off the bench — like Wagler — to begin his rookie season, but should play significant minutes off the bench.
